key_insight: Combining smartphone transillumination, 3D geometry, and physics-informed features classified woody breast severity with approximately 90% test accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a potentially accessible, non-destructive alternative to subjective palpation and specialized inspection equipment for chicken fillet quality assessment.
method: Acquire RAW transillumination images and 3D point clouds with an iPhone 16 Pro.
Extract 91 features: 14 image-derived, 76 geometric, and one Beer–Lambert attenuation feature.
Combine Fusion-DGCNN, XGBoost, and physics-guided logistic regression in a multimodal ensemble.
evidence_signal: Among 267 fillets spanning normal, mild, and severe woody breast, multimodal test accuracy reached approximately 90% versus 82% for 2D-only models; severe tissue showed approximately 26% greater attenuation per unit thickness than normal tissue.
watch_item: Generalization beyond the 267-fillet dataset and robustness across devices, lighting conditions, and processing environments remain to be established.
paper_title: Smartphone-Enabled Depth-Aware Transillumination Imaging for Detection of Chicken Breast Fillet Myopathies in Chicken Fillets
